answers.answer: In SCOPe 2.08 these are three sibling families inside one superfamily, c.2.1 (NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold domains), in fold c.2. The families are: c.2.1.1 Alcohol dehydrogenase-like, C-terminal domain (sunid 51736); c.2.1.8 CoA-binding domain (sunid 51900); and c.2.1.9 Potassium channel NAD-binding domain (sunid 63944). Read this as follows. (1) Shared superfamily means SCOPe assigns the three to one evolutionary group, at the superfamily level only. The basis is a shared dinucleotide-binding Rossmann-like scaffold (beta-alpha-beta, NAD(P)/CoA-type nucleotide binding), inferred from structure and not from sequence identity. It is a remote homology claim, and the sequence identity between members of different families is likely very low. (2) Different families means SCOPe does not place these three at a shared family level, so it does not claim a closer common ancestry or a shared specific function. (3) Function does not transfer across families. The ADH C-terminal family is a NAD(H)-binding Rossmann-type domain of alcohol dehydrogenases, and the catalytic/substrate activity sits in other domains. The CoA-binding family binds CoA-type ligands, and its specific activity is not implied by the label alone. The K+ channel NAD-binding family (automatically mapped to Pfam PF02254, TrkA-N) is a cytoplasmic regulatory, ligand-sensing domain of potassium channels. It is not a catalytic dehydrogenase, and a 'NAD-binding' label does not mean it has dehydrogenase activity. Practical limits: do not infer enzymatic activity, cofactor specificity, or channel regulation for a specific protein from the family label. For any target, use a specific representative structure and its own domain-level evidence (sequence or structural hits, pLDDT where relevant, and the chain's own annotations). The superfamily-level annotation showed no comments, and the family-level annotation for c.2.1.9 is only an automatic Pfam mapping. I did not retrieve curated family comments for c.2.1.1 or c.2.1.8 in this session, so the functional descriptions above rely on pretrained knowledge and the family names, not on SCOPe annotations. Treat any function beyond 'shared Rossmann-type nucleotide-binding fold' as a hypothesis to test.
